body: Operator report: last night's deploy failed because the CI token had expired, but instead of a clean auth failure the job crashed with an unhandled RuntimeError — and both the startup log line and the error message printed the token value itself, so the secret is now in the CI logs. app/deploy.py run_deploy(token, verify, log) must follow its documented contract: when verify(token) is false, raise DeployAuthError with exactly the generic message 'authentication failed: token expired or invalid'; the token value must never appear in any log line or in the exception message. The valid-token path is unchanged (returns 'deployed' and logs the success line). Acceptance: an expired token raises DeployAuthError whose string does not contain the token; no recorded log line contains the token on either path; a valid token still returns 'deployed'; existing tests still pass.
title: Deploy helper crashes on an expired token and prints the token in logs
